budget.title: A daily budget you set
budget.body: The most that can be spent in a day, decided by you.

connections.title: Checked connections
connections.body: Facebook, Instagram and Google Ads accounts are checked with the platform before anything is saved.

knowledge.q: Do I need to know marketing?
knowledge.a: No. GrowthOS reads your site and does the professional work - goals, ads, landing pages, audiences and keywords. You decide: approve, ask for a change or reject.

spend.q: Will you spend money without asking me?
spend.a: No. Every ad is created paused, and it only starts running when you approve it, within the daily budget you set.

platforms.a: On Facebook and Instagram, and on Google (search and images). You connect your ad accounts once, and every connection is checked with the platform.

developers.q: I'm a developer - is there an API?
developers.a: Yes. You can send events, customers and sales from your site or your server, with a script for the browser and an SDK for Node.

AuditLog.title: Audit log
AuditLog.chainValid: Chain verified — {count} entries, no tampering detected.
AuditLog.chainBrokenHashMismatchTitle: Integrity check failed: this entry was changed after it was recorded.
AuditLog.chainBrokenHashMismatchMeaning: What it means: the entry's stored content no longer matches the fingerprint taken when it was written. GrowthOS never edits an entry once it is recorded, so it was changed directly in the database, outside the app.
AuditLog.chainBrokenChainBreakTitle: Integrity check failed: the entry recorded just before this one is missing or was changed.
AuditLog.chainBrokenChainBreakMeaning: What it means: this entry points back to an earlier entry that no longer exists in its original form - it was deleted, or edited and re-fingerprinted, directly in the database. Changes saved at the same moment cannot cause this.
AuditLog.chainBrokenNextSteps: What to do: don't edit or delete any more entries, so the evidence is preserved. Compare this entry with your backups to see what changed and who had database access at that time, and contact GrowthOS support with the entry ID.
AuditLog.chainBranchedTitle: Chain verified - {count} entries, none changed or removed from the middle of the log.
AuditLog.chainBranchedBody: {forks, plural, one {At one point} other {At # points}}, several changes were saved at the same moment and each linked to the same earlier entry, so the log branches there ({branched, plural, one {# entry sits} other {# entries sit}} on a side branch). This happens when many changes are made at once, for example a plugin registering its metrics, and is not a sign of tampering. Every branched entry still verifies on its own; as with the newest entry, removing an entry at the end of a side branch would not be detectable.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: GrowthOS is a growth analytics and advertising platform. This policy explains what data GrowthOS handles - in particular when an organization connects a Facebook (Meta) ad account - and how that data is used, protected and deleted.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: The account details you sign in with (name and email). The data your organization sends or connects for analysis, such as events, campaigns and ad results. When an administrator uses "Connect with Facebook": an access token issued by Meta, and the ids and names of the ad accounts and Facebook Pages the administrator chooses. We do not collect friends lists, messages or personal posts.

use.title: How we use it
use.body: Only to provide what your organization uses GrowthOS for: showing growth analytics, and creating and managing the ads a member asks GrowthOS to create. Ads GrowthOS creates on Meta or Google are always created paused, so nothing runs or spends until you turn it on in the platform. We do not sell data and do not use it to advertise ourselves.

protect.title: How it is protected
protect.body: Access tokens and other connection secrets are encrypted before they are stored, with keys kept in Google Cloud Secret Manager, and are decrypted only in memory for the request that needs them. Data is hosted on Google Cloud. Only members of your organization with the right permission can see or use a connection, and changes are recorded in an audit log.

share.title: Who we share it with
share.body: Only the platforms you connect, and only to do what you asked (for example, sending an ad to Meta's Marketing API or to Google Ads); and the providers that run GrowthOS - Google Cloud for hosting, and Google's Gemini models, which write ad plans and generate images and videos from what you tell it. No one else.

deletion.title: Keeping and deleting data
deletion.body: A connection's data is kept while the connection exists. To delete what GrowthOS holds from Facebook, an organization administrator removes the connection's access in GrowthOS (Resource library, then the Meta credential), which deletes the stored token at once; you can also remove GrowthOS in Facebook under Settings, Apps and websites, which revokes its access. Any other data is deleted within 30 days of your organization asking us to delete it.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For questions or deletion requests, contact your organization's GrowthOS administrator, or the GrowthOS team through the support page inside the app.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: When this policy changes, the date at the top of this page changes with it.

overview.title: Build on GrowthOS
overview.intro: Send your product's events, customers and revenue to GrowthOS, read metrics back, and connect AI agents over MCP - from the browser, from your server, or from any language over HTTP.
overview.testedNote: Every sample on these pages runs against a GrowthOS test environment before it ships. Start with test keys (gos_test_, gos_pk_test_): nothing touches production data until you switch to live keys.

cards.quickStart: From zero to a verified event in five steps, in a test environment.

cards.serverSide: The Node.js SDK: events, customers and measures with batching, retries and a result for every record.

environments.title: Projects and environments
environments.body: Every project has three environments: dev, staging and prod. A key belongs to one environment, and the records it sends land only there.

keys.title: Keys
keys.body: A browser key (gos_pk_...) is public: it can only send events, and only from the domains you list. A server key (gos_test_... for dev and staging, gos_live_... for prod) stays on your server. The key decides the project and the environment - there is no project id in your code.

schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.body: Every event, entity and measure name is registered first, with the fields it carries. A record with an unregistered name or an undeclared field is quarantined with the reason, and the rest of its batch still lands.

identity.title: Identity
identity.body: anon_id (the visitor) and customer_id (the signed-in customer) ride inside properties. Sending the browser's anon_id with the server's signup ties the signup to the campaign of the visit.

idempotency.title: Safe retries
idempotency.body: Every event carries your own event_id. Sending the same id again is reported as a duplicate, not stored twice, so retrying a failed request is always safe.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.intro: Five steps from nothing to a verified event, all in a test environment. You need a GrowthOS project; the samples use curl and read the server key from the GROWTHOS_API_KEY environment variable.
quickStart.step1Body: Open your project in GrowthOS, switch the environment to dev, and on the Keys page create a server key with ingest.write, schema.write and mcp.read, and a browser key for your site's domains (http://localhost is allowed for testing). Test keys start with gos_test_ and gos_pk_test_.
quickStart.step1Env: Keep the server key in an environment variable - never in code or in a page:
quickStart.step2Body: Declare every event, entity and measure you will send, with its fields. This manifest registers the ones the guides use - touchpoint (GrowthOS's own visit schema), signup, cta_click, a customer entity and an mrr measure; replace them with your own. It goes through MCP's apply_schema_manifest, or use the Schemas page in the app. Schemas are project-wide, so they are ready for prod too.
quickStart.step3Body: One signup event in the exact wire shape. The response says how many records were accepted, quarantined (with the reason) or duplicates.
quickStart.step4Title: 4. Add the browser and server SDKs
quickStart.step4Body: On your site, the browser SDK sends a touchpoint at the start of each visit and the events you track. On your server, the Node.js SDK sends signups, customers and revenue. Any other language calls the HTTP API.
quickStart.step5Body: Ask GrowthOS what really arrived for each schema: receiving, quarantined (with the reason), registered but no data or not registered. The Installation page in the app shows the same, and can listen live while you click through your site.
quickStart.liveBody: Create live keys in the prod environment (gos_live_..., gos_pk_live_...), swap them into your configuration and run the same check against prod. Nothing else needs to be registered again.

clientSide.title: Client side: the browser SDK
clientSide.intro: About 9 KB, no dependencies, never blocks the page. It sends a touchpoint at the start of each visit - campaign, ad click id, landing page and referrer - and the events you track.
clientSide.keyBody: Create a browser key for the environment and list your site's domains. It can only send events, and only from those domains - a page anywhere else gets 403. http://localhost is allowed, so a test key works on your own machine.
clientSide.secretWarning: Never put a server key (gos_test_... or gos_live_...) in a page. GrowthOS refuses a server key sent from a browser.
clientSide.snippetBody: Paste it once into the head of every page. It loads the SDK asynchronously and queues calls until it arrives, so early track calls are never lost. Replace the key with your browser key.
clientSide.npmBody: For single-page apps and bundlers. The package is served by GrowthOS; pin the versioned file.
clientSide.apiTrack: track(event, properties) - send an event. The name must be a registered event schema, and every property must be declared on it.
clientSide.apiIdentify: identify(customerId) - after signup or login: later events carry the customer id.
clientSide.apiReset: reset() - on logout: forgets the customer and starts a new anonymous visitor.
clientSide.apiAnon: getAnonId() - the visitor id. Send it to your server at signup so the signup is credited to this visit.
clientSide.apiPage: pageViews: true - sends page_view with the path on load and on every in-app navigation. Register a page_view schema with a path field first.
clientSide.apiFlush: Events are sent in batches (10 events or 1 second), and whatever is left when the page is hidden goes out with sendBeacon. flush() sends now.
clientSide.consentBody: Start in pending and nothing is stored or sent until consent is granted; denied drops what waited and clears the stored ids.
clientSide.relayBody: If your page may only call its own origin, let the browser SDK post to your own route and forward from there with the server key. The relay forwards only the event names you allow, with size limits.
clientSide.verifyBody: With a browser key, run this in the browser console on your site. It prints whether each schema is receiving, quarantined (with the reason) or not registered - from what really arrived. A rejected record is also logged to the console with its reason.

serverSide.title: Server side: the Node.js SDK
serverSide.intro: Node.js 18 or newer, no dependencies. Batching, retries on 429 / 5xx / network errors, a result for every record, a relay for browser events, backfill helpers and an installation check.
serverSide.installBody: The SDK is served by GrowthOS. Install the versioned file, so your lockfile never sees its content change:
serverSide.exampleBody: A complete script: it reads the key from GROWTHOS_API_KEY, sends one event, one customer and one measure, prints what happened to each record and runs the installation check. Run it as an ES module (for example node send.mjs).
serverSide.resultsBody: flush(), shutdown() and the immediate sendEvents() / sendEntities() / sendMeasures() return the accepted, quarantined and duplicate counts and every record that was not accepted, with its reasons. In a serverless function, call flush() before returning; before a process exits, call shutdown().
serverSide.idBody: eventId(...parts) turns your own data into a stable id, so a retried job is reported as a duplicate instead of being counted twice. Send every attribute of a customer each time: an entity upsert replaces the whole row.
serverSide.cliTitle: Check from the terminal or CI
serverSide.cliBody: The SDK ships a growthos command. Exit code 0 means everything expected is arriving, 1 means something needs attention, 2 means the check itself failed - so it fits a deploy pipeline.
serverSide.otherBody: Every SDK call is one HTTPS request with a JSON body - Python, PHP, Go or anything else uses the HTTP API directly.

api.title: HTTP API
api.intro: Every call is HTTPS with a bearer key and a JSON body. These are the same endpoints the SDKs use.
api.authBody: Send the key as Authorization: Bearer .... The key decides the organization, project and environment - there is no project id in the URL. All paths start with the base URL:

endpoints.entities: Upsert entities of one type - always the whole row.
endpoints.validate: Check records against your schemas exactly as ingest would, without storing anything.
endpoints.batch: The result of every record in a batch.
endpoints.verify: The installation check: what really arrived for each expected schema.
endpoints.metricsQuery: Query a metric as a time series.
endpoints.mcp: The MCP server (JSON-RPC) for AI agents.

api.eventsBody: Records go in a top-level batch array. event_id, event and ts are required; the schema's fields go in properties, together with anon_id and customer_id.
api.entitiesBody: One request carries one entity type. Send the whole row every time - an upsert replaces it, so an attribute you leave out is erased.
api.measuresBody: Pre-aggregated numbers, such as a day's revenue: the number is a top-level value and the breakdown goes in dimensions. Re-sending the same aggregate is idempotent.
api.responseBody: 202 with the counts of accepted, quarantined and duplicate records; every record that was not accepted is listed with its status and reasons (for example missing_required_field:plan, unregistered_field:..., field_type_mismatch:... or schema_not_registered). The batch endpoint returns the result of every record.
api.metricsBody: Register a metric (here through MCP's register_metric, which needs metrics.write), list the catalog and query a time series. New records reach the warehouse in its hourly refresh, so a fresh project returns an empty series at first.
api.contractBody: The ingest contract as an OpenAPI 3.1 document - request envelopes, the batch response and the rules a JSON schema cannot express. No key needed.
api.errorsBody: 400 malformed request - 401 missing or unknown key - 403 a scope the key lacks, or a browser key used outside its domains - 413 too large - 429 rate limited: wait for Retry-After - 5xx retry with backoff. Records are never half-stored: retrying with the same ids is always safe.

mcp.title: MCP for AI agents
mcp.intro: GrowthOS is a Model Context Protocol server. An agent can read schemas, metrics and funnels, check the installation, register schemas and metrics, manage goals and segments, run the Ad Studio and propose automation changes - with the same permissions, limits and audit log as the app.
mcp.endpointBody: One URL for every project: the credential decides the organization, project and environment. The server is stateless - every request authenticates on its own.
mcp.authBody: Interactive clients such as Claude Desktop and claude.ai sign in with OAuth - there is no secret to copy. Agents and scripts use a server key with mcp.read, plus schema.write, metrics.write or dashboards.write for the tools that change things. Approving automation always needs a person and is never available to a key.
mcp.claudeBody: Add a custom connector with the endpoint URL above. You are sent to GrowthOS to sign in and choose the project, and the GrowthOS tools appear in your next conversation.

testing.envBody: Test keys belong to dev or staging; live keys to prod. Records land only in the key's environment, so test data never mixes with production numbers. Schemas and metrics are shared across all three.

testing.loop2: Open the Installation page and press Listen live, or run the verify call below.

reasons.quota_exceeded: today's AI limit is used up, it resets tomorrow
reasons.provider_error: the AI service did not answer, try again in a minute
reasons.invalid_output: the AI's answer was not usable, ask for a change to try again
reasons.no_images: no image passed the quality check, ask for a change to try again
reasons.publish_failed: Facebook and Instagram did not accept it, check your ad account connection
reasons.auth_failed: Facebook and Instagram no longer accept the saved connection, reconnect your ad account in Ad platform connections
reasons.no_secret: your Facebook and Instagram connection has no saved login, reconnect your ad account in Ad platform connections
reasons.account_action_required: Facebook needs you to verify your ad account in Ads Manager (adsmanager.facebook.com) first, then try again
reasons.meta_account_restricted: Facebook has restricted your ad account, so no ads can be created. Open Ads Manager (adsmanager.facebook.com) to see why and fix it, or connect a different ad account
reasons.rejected: Facebook and Instagram refused the ad, ask for a change to the ads or check your ad account
reasons.rate_limited: the AI service is busy, try again in a minute
reasons.refused: the AI declined to write this, ask for a change worded differently
reasons.provider_billing: the AI service is not available on our side right now, trying again will not help - please contact GrowthOS support
reasons.not_configured: the AI service is not set up on our side yet, trying again will not help - please contact GrowthOS support
reasons.upload_failed: the upload to Facebook and Instagram did not go through, try again in a minute
reasons.cancelled: it was stopped before it finished, ask for a change to try again
reasons.nothing_to_revise: there was nothing to change yet, reload the page and try again
reasons.platform_busy: the ad platform is receiving too many requests right now, try again in a few minutes
reasons.timed_out: it took too long and was given up, ask for a change to try again
reasons.no_concepts: the AI could not come up with ideas for this, ask for a change worded differently
reasons.generic: something went wrong, try again in a minute
